preview: Interview and internship experience details at UBS for a Software Development Intern role by Darshan Shelar.
content: Public Role: Software Development Intern Stipend: 40,000/MONTH Location: Mumbai/Pune Criteria: 7+ CPI 70%+ in 10th and 12th Interview + Internship Experience Darshan Shelar- Btech in Information Technology Timeline : 1. PPT: 2. Online Test: 24th January 2023 (5:00 pm -7:00 pm) 3. Interview: 31st January 2023 Online Test An online test for 2 hours was conducted on the Hackerrank platform. It consisted of MCQ part and Coding part (You can navigate to previous questions). Preparation: Keep practicing on coding platforms like codechef, Leetcode, 450DSA, Striver sheet, etc. For MCQs, make sure you solve some logical and quantitative questions. Rest, DBMS, OS, CN and DSA will be from your curriculum so make sure you are thorough in that. General tips: First try to solve the coding question, and then move to MCQs. MCQs: There were 60 MCQs, Questions were on aptitude, logical reasoning, quantitative analysis, DBMS OS CN, and some basic DSA. Coding question: There was only one coding question, Languages were C, C++ and Java. Online Test: Coding question A company wants all of its employees to focus in cyber security and hence regularly change their passwords. Given two binary string passwords s and t of equal length. Each string represents a binary Integer where the first character represents the most significant bit of number. You can rearrange the characters of t in any order you want. The task is to maximise the value of bitwise XOR of s and t. Return maximum possible XOR as a binary string of length the same as the input strings For example, s = ”0011110”, t = “1111000”. It is optimal to rearrange the characters of t to “1100011”. The bitwise XOR of s and t would be “1111101”. Hence the answer is “1111101”. Interview Interview consisted of only one round. It was for about 40 to 60 minutes. Preparation: You should be able to explain your whole resume. Keep practicing on coding platforms like codechef, Leetcode, etc. In interviews, only easy problems are asked. Go through OS and DBMS questions on Interviewbits. Practice SQL queries, specially the join ones. Make sure you are aware of all OOPs concepts specifically the inheritance and classes part. Prepare all the known sorting algorithms with their pseudocode (Bubble sort, Insertion sort and Selection sort are simplest and most asked ones). Mention 3 to 4 projects in resume. practice for the data structures along with pseudocode (Stack, Queue, Linked List, trees and graphs and their functions and algorithms). Go through Interviewbit site’s frequently asked questions General tips: Be confident and clear. If you don’t know the answer, just sat so. Make sure that you are not saying any fake/unstudied terms. Because they will cross question you. Interview: Questions asked 1. DSA question- explain stack and heap, Implement Stack and it’s functions (pseudo code). 2. Sorting question- give names of some sorting algorithms you know, give pseudocode and step by step explanation + working for any one of your choice. 3. Coding question- you are given a string consisting of many small case alphabets, find the alphabet which had maximum count. 4. Project question- explain projects mentioned in your resume, give final output, use case diagram, some functions and technologies used, the reason why you’ve used the particular technology and give it’s alternatives (eg. If you have used MariaDB database, state why you have used that, Mention the other technologies available like MongoDB, and the benefits of MariaDB over MongoDB) 5. Theory questions- some basic questions on OS and DBMS, a complex sql query was also asked. Internship Experience It was an amazing experience interning with UBS.I got to learn a lot of new things and interact with many individuals across this summer program. There were a lot of events, mandatory training sessions which were conducted along with our assigned work. I worked on web automation part using python. Here, I’ve learned more about selenium library and table scraping stuff. I was assigned with 3 projects. The role and project differs from person to person. My manager, mentor, and buddy were all very supportive and helpful. They made sure that I was able to get up to speed quickly and that I had everything I needed to succeed. Not only them, even those working around with me were friendly. I came to know a lot about Software Development Life Cycle, the deadline management part and various other activities. In the final weeks, each intern need to give a presentation sharing his projects and experience in UBS office. Overall, my internship at UBS was an amazing experience. I learned a lot, made great connections, and had a lot of fun. I'm so grateful for the opportunity and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who is looking for a challenging and rewarding internship. Internship Experience: Do’s and Don’ts Make sure you are in close contact with other interns too. This will ensure that you do not miss any event or other stuff. Keep your buddy updated on what progress you make everyday. Make sure that you prioritize your tasks properly and manage deadlines. In the final presentation, you must mention the things you learned in UBS and not just project work. Keep it more presentable, make use of flowcharts, tables and various animations. If you face any difficulty, just seek for any colleague. They will surely help you. Do not share any kind of confidential data with others. KEEP YOUR LINE MAGER/MENTOR HAPPY He is the one who will give your feedback and your ppo will be based on his feedback.
